block_05_direct_answer.title: Direct answer
block_05_direct_answer.body_html: The best rental-income area depends on demand, total cost and exit flexibility. For villa buyers, compare realistic rents, service charges, vacancy risk, competing supply, purchase price and the depth of the tenant market. Use current listings and transaction evidence before treating any district or property as the strongest income option.

items.answer: The best rental-income area depends on demand, total cost and exit flexibility. For villa buyers, define who is likely to rent the property, why they choose the area and whether that tenant base is broad enough to support demand.
items.question: Which areas should I compare for rental income?

items.answer: A rental-income area should combine tenant depth with sustainable ownership economics. Compare realistic rents from similar units and buildings rather than relying only on advertised asking rents or a projected headline return.
items.question: How should I choose an area for rental income?

items.answer: Rental demand should be checked through realistic tenant activity, not headline yield claims. Model periods without rent, tenant changes and leasing friction rather than assuming continuous occupancy throughout the holding period.
items.question: How should I assess rental demand?

items.answer: Investment logic should connect the purchase price to realistic income, costs and exit options. Model lower rent, slower resale, higher costs or a longer holding period to see whether the investment still works under less favourable conditions.
items.question: How should I assess the investment case?

items.answer: Capital-growth area selection should focus on durable demand and improving fundamentals, not forecasts alone. The case depends on future appreciation without enough evidence from current demand and fundamentals. Treat projected appreciation as uncertain and compare downside scenarios before choosing a location.
